title: feat(cli): os migrate text-scalars rewrites numbers and booleans stored raw on text fields, reports SQLite "N.0" text (#29702)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8Q2NNUVcGoRpeRy6bmuAdsV)_
Fixes #29702

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:新增 `os migrate text-scalars`,把 #29241 之前写进文本类字段(spec 的 `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`)的旧值一次性处理:内存驱动保存的原始数字/布尔改写成 `String(value)`;SQLite 的 `"42.0"`/`"1.0"`/`"0.0"` 判不了,按对象和字段列出,永不改写。
- 为什么改:旧行与新行存成两种形态,`{ t: "42" }` 筛不到旧行、读出来是旧形态、唯一文本字段上新 `"42"` 与旧 `42`/`"42.0"` 不冲突(本 PR 实测,见 Why)。
- 风险与回滚:默认只读演练;`--apply` 需 `--yes`,只改原始数字/布尔,写入口拒收的行(唯一冲突、格式不再通过)逐行记失败、整行不动、继续走;回滚即撤 PR,已改写的值与新写入同形。
- 先看:① `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/text-scalars.ts` 的 `decideTextScalar` 与 `textScalarFields`;② 同文件 `migrateTextScalars` 的整行改写与逐行失败;③ `text-scalars.integration.test.ts`(真实 SQLite)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration src/commands/migrate/text-scalars.integration.test.ts`,应见 28/28 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **New command `os migrate text-scalars`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/text-scalars.ts`), the data half of #29241. It walks every text-family field, by keyset on `id`. The type set is read from the spec export `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), the set the #29241 door (`normalizeNumericStringRow` in `record-validator.ts`) reads; no type is listed in code. The field scope is the door's walk: a `readonly` field is in; otherwise an engine lifecycle column (`ENGINE_LIFECYCLE_COLUMNS` from `@objectstack/core`) and a `system` field are out; the key (`id`, a `primaryKey` field) is always out because it addresses the update.
- **The decision (`decideTextScalar`)**, per stored value:
  - a raw number or boolean (driver-memory's face) is decidable by type and becomes `String(value)`, exactly the string the door writes for the same input;
  - a SQLite REAL text form (`"42.0"`, `"1.0"`, `"0.0"`, `"-3.0"`, and the exponent form `"1.0e+21"` SQLite prints from 1e15 up) is reported `sqlite-real-text`, never rewritten: a text field declares no values, so it may be the old number or a string a client typed (the `free-field` case of `os migrate option-codes`);
  - every other string, `null` and every non-scalar is left alone.
- **The walk (`migrateTextScalars`)**: dry run by default (read-only boot, writes nothing); `--apply` (with `--yes`, or the prompt) rewrites each row's raw scalars in one engine update under the system context. A row the door refuses (a unique collision with a row already holding the string, or a string the field's format no longer admits) is a per-row failure, left whole, and the walk goes on; a failure exits 1. `--object` narrows the walk and refuses an undeclared name; `--max-records` bounds it; `--apply` refuses a SQLite file another process holds unless `--force`. No deployment flag: a re-run that reports zero to rewrite is the verification.
- **A sibling of `option-codes`, not an arm of it.** That command's name, help text and clean verdict ("every stored option value is a code string") are about option fields, and its decision is a lookup in declared codes that a text field does not have; folding text fields in would change what an already-run `option-codes` means to an operator. One step per value class is the family's precedent (`blank-single-values`, `option-codes`). Not part of `value-shapes` either, which stays read-only (#29431, ruling 6588116815).
- **Registered at the three family sites**: `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts` (no-write and write rows), `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` (no stray stdout under `--json`), `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` (`--apply` without `--yes` exits 1 before the boot).
- **Docs**: a row in the `os migrate` table and an `os migrate text-scalars` section in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/29702-migrate-text-scalars.md`, `@objectstack/cli` patch.

## Why

Measured on `origin/main` 87956dcc by writing rows below the door, as the pre-#29241 door handed them to the driver (`driver.create`), then asking the engine. Field `t` is `text`, `u` is a unique `text`.

| | SQLite (driver-sql, better-sqlite3) | driver-memory (InMemoryDriver) | Postgres 16 (driver-sql, pg) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| stored `42` / `true` / `false` / `1e21` | TEXT `"42.0"` / `"1.0"` / `"0.0"` / `"1.0e+21"` | raw `42` / `true` / `false` / `1e+21` | text `"42"` / `"true"` / `"false"` / `"1e+21"` |
| stored `-1.5` / `0.1+0.2` | `"-1.5"` / `"0.30000000000000004"` (already the string) | raw numbers | same strings |
| read of row `42` | `"42.0"` | `42` | `"42"` |
| filter `{ t: "42" }` | misses | misses | finds |
| filter `{ t: 42 }` | finds | finds | finds |
| filter `{ t: "true" }` on row `true` | misses (`"1.0"` finds) | misses | finds |
| today's door, `insert { t: 42 }` | stores `"42"` | stores `"42"` | stores `"42"` |
| unique `insert { u: "42" }` beside old `u = 42` | admitted (no collision) | admitted (no collision) | refused `DUPLICATE_RECORD` |

So SQLite and driver-memory hold two stored shapes for one value; Postgres already stored the string the door writes today and has nothing to migrate. MySQL: NOT MEASURED, reason: no MySQL server in this container (Postgres 16 binaries were present and a throwaway cluster was started on a random port and stopped after the run).

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/text-scalars.integration.test.ts`, on a real `ObjectQL` + sqlite `SqlDriver`, 28 tests:

- the decision table (20 rows): raw scalars rewrite to `String(value)` (`42`, `-1.5`, `0`, `true`, `false`, `1e21`); `"42.0"`, `"1.0"`, `"0.0"`, `"-3.0"`, `"1.0e+21"` report; `"42"`, `"-1.5"`, `"hello"`, `"42.0 is a version"`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, an object, an array are left alone;
- the field scope: all twelve spec text types, `readonly` in, key / lifecycle / non-readonly `system` out, `select` / `number` / `json` / `secret` / `lookup` out;
- SQLite `"N.0"`: red before (stored and read as `"42.0"`, `{ t: "42" }` misses, a unique `"42"` is admitted); a dry run reports per object and field and writes nothing; `--apply` leaves every `"N.0"` as stored and reports it again;
- the rewrite arm, driver-memory's face: driver-memory itself is not a test backend here (its consumers are a closed census, `check:driver-memory-census`), so the arm is pinned by the decision table and its walk is driven on the real sqlite engine through `memoryFace`, whose reads hand back the raw scalar driver-memory kept for a row whose column is still unwritten and whose writes are the real engine's: a dry run counts and writes nothing; `--apply` writes `"42"` / `"true"` / `"false"` / `"7"`, `{ t: "42" }` then finds the row, a unique `"42"` then collides, and a re-run reads zero; a unique collision with a row already holding `"42"` is a per-row failure that leaves the row whole while the rest of the walk lands; `objects` narrows the walk.

## Acceptance notes

- A raw scalar the door now refuses as a string (for example `true` on an `email` field, measured: `mail must be a valid email address`) surfaces as a per-row failure carrying the door's message, and the row's other text fields are not rewritten either, as in `option-codes` ("a row never ends half-migrated"). Such a value could not have passed the pre-#29241 door either, which judged `String(value)` by the same rules, so it needs a rule change or a write below the door to exist.
- SQLite stored a number from 1e15 up in exponent form (`"1.0e+21"`), which is reported with the other `"N.0"` forms; the digits lost there were lost at write time.
